intro_script: Welcome to the Robotics Digest for October 31, 2026. We cover 29 updates, including big moves in warehouse automation, autonomous factory building, and driverless truck scaling. Tune in for the latest.

items.title: Walmart expands Symbotic warehouse automation deal with $6 billion commitment
items.summary: Symbotic and Walmart have expanded their commercial agreement, committing approximately $6 billion for further automation. This deal will bring advanced AI-enabled robotics capabilities to 25 US regional distribution centers and support global supply chain growth. Symbotic's solutions, like BreakPack and SymMicro, use AI to optimize the movement of inventory. Walmart aims to use this expanded automation to improve e-commerce inventory management, storage capacity, and product flow. Ultimately, this partnership seeks to enhance customer service by increasing speed and reliability across the supply chain.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Walmart expands Symbotic warehouse automation deal with $6 billion commitment. This report details an expanded commercial agreement between Walmart and Symbotic, involving a commitment of approximately six billion dollars for further automation implementation. The agreement will introduce advanced artificial intelligence enabled robotics capabilities across twenty-five United States regional distribution centers to facilitate global supply chain expansion. Symbotic’s solutions, including BreakPack and SymMicro, utilize artificial intelligence to optimize the movement of inventory within these facilities. Walmart intends to leverage this expanded automation to enhance e-commerce inventory management, increase storage capacity, and refine product flow. This partnership is structured to improve customer service through increased speed and reliability throughout the supply chain operations. This development signals continued integration of advanced robotics and artificial intelligence into large-scale logistics operations.

items.title: Foundry Robotics raises $100 million to build ‘America’s first autonomous factory for assembly’
items.summary: Foundry Robotics secured a $100 million Series A funding round led by Marlinspike Partners to build "America's first autonomous factory for assembly." The company builds autonomous factories that combine AI-powered robotic cells with manufacturing expertise. Foundry offers a manufacturing-as-a-service model, allowing customers to go from design to production quickly without retooling. The company focuses on assembling complex electro-mechanical products for the defense and commercial industries. Through its technology, Foundry aims to revitalize US manufacturing by providing scalable and flexible assembly capacity.

The company concentrates its technological application on assembling complex electro-mechanical products for both the defense and commercial sectors, intending to stimulate U.S. manufacturing by offering flexible and scalable assembly capacity. This development signals a focus on leveraging advanced robotics to redefine industrial production methodologies. Future developments in autonomous manufacturing will be closely observed by industry analysts.

items.title: Aurora outlines plan to scale to 30,000 driverless trucks
items.summary: Aurora Innovation aims to have over 30,000 driverless trucks operational by 2030 in the United States. The company expects 200 driverless trucks to be operating through Transport as a Service agreements by 2026, with further deliveries scheduled in 2027. Trucks using Aurora's system have completed over 500,000 driverless miles, with customers averaging over 225,000 miles annually. Aurora is increasing hardware production, with Roush currently upfitting trucks at a rate of 20 per week. The autonomous driving technology is currently integrated into International LT Series trucks and is being developed for future integration into PACCAR trucks.

This development indicates ongoing progress in the commercialization and integration of autonomous driving systems within the commercial trucking sector.

items.title: AgiBot revenue nears 2 billion yuan as humanoid shipments rise
items.summary: AgiBot generated nearly 2 billion yuan in revenue in the first half of 2026, reflecting rising humanoid shipments. The company shipped 9,700 humanoid robots in that period and claimed a 43.1 percent share of global shipments. AgiBot emphasized that its figures demonstrate the ability to manufacture at scale and deploy robots effectively, emphasizing the need for supply chains and maintenance. Unitree Robotics also reported strong financial results, with revenue growing significantly in the first nine months of 2026. Revenue growth is attributed to increased manufacturing capacity, expanded domestic and overseas applications, and the integration of long-term service solutions alongside hardware sales.

items.title: Humanoid expands collaboration with Nvidia to power its next generation of humanoid robots
items.summary: Humanoid is partnering with Nvidia to develop the computing foundation for next-generation AI-powered humanoid robots. They are developing a high-performance robotic edge runtime to allow robots to run sophisticated AI onboard for real-time perception and response. This integration includes Nvidia Jetson Thor, Isaac OS, Holoscan Sensor Bridge, and SDK to process sensor data and coordinate control. This collaboration aims to streamline the architecture and reduce latency for real-world deployment of autonomous robots. Ultimately, the partnership seeks to unlock new levels of autonomy for humanoid robots.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Humanoid expands collaboration with Nvidia to power its next generation of humanoid robots". This report details a partnership between Humanoid and Nvidia to develop the computing foundation for forthcoming humanoid robots, focusing on a high-performance robotic edge runtime for onboard artificial intelligence processing. The collaboration involves the integration of technologies such as the Nvidia Jetson Thor, Isaac OS, Holoscan Sensor Bridge, and associated Software Development Kits to facilitate the processing of sensor data and coordination of control. This integration aims to streamline the system architecture and decrease latency for the real-world deployment of autonomous robots. This partnership seeks to unlock new levels of autonomy for humanoid robotic systems. The development signals a significant step in creating more capable and responsive autonomous robotic hardware.

items.title: Maximo Robotics completes 300,000 tasks in utility-scale solar projects
items.summary: Maximo Robotics has completed over 300,000 construction tasks using its US-made, physical-AI robotics systems for utility-scale solar projects. Crew members working with Max 4.0 systems achieved 2.5 times their manual installation rates per person per shift hour. The company operates on a performance-based robotics-as-a-service model where customers pay per completed task. This deployment is helping electricity companies meet energy demand in a labor-constrained market. The platform combines AI models, robotics, and operational intelligence to automate construction tasks across various domains.

items.title: AstraQua secures $1.3 million NASA contract for physical AI
items.summary: AstraQua secured a $1.3 million NASA contract to advance its AstraSense technology for electric and hybrid-electric aircraft. This work focuses on developing Physical AI that incorporates predictive health and operational self-awareness for autonomous systems. AstraSense allows machines to understand their own condition to make safer, real-time decisions, enabling collaborative task management. The technology aims to facilitate adaptation among robot teams, such as in inspection scenarios. This research emphasizes low-power onboard intelligence and health-informed reasoning for autonomous operations.

items.title: Why Automated Cells Are Pulling Inspection Onto the Shop Floor
items.summary: Automated cells are bringing inspection closer to the shop floor to improve efficiency. As automation grows, moving Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMMs) next to production allows for rapid part checking. This proximity shortens the feedback loop, enabling immediate adjustments to machining processes. Shared data standards like MTConnect allow robots and inspection equipment to communicate effectively. This integration enables real-time quality control, catching variations early and increasing production confidence.

The shuttle is designed to offer an economically viable entry point into warehouse automation by fitting into existing facilities. This technology allows for increased storage density without major structural changes, providing a path toward further automation. The collaboration enables customers to modernize brownfield warehouses gradually, integrating shuttle technology with other automation solutions.

items.title: Welcome, Pantheon Hand!
items.summary: Pantheon Hand is Stella Robot's flagship tendon-driven robotic hand, featuring a lightweight design with electric motors located outside the hand for mass reduction. It has a weight of 0.29 kg, dimensions of 230 × 190 × 50 mm, and a five-finger configuration utilizing single side pull cables with automatic tension adjustment. The hand received an overall score of 7/10, with a higher rating for Degrees of Freedom (4/5) than for Strength (3/5). The design emphasizes dexterity and joint freedom while maintaining a moderate strength assessment. The product is currently in production and is priced at USD 3,500.

items.title: Welcome, Mantis Standart!
items.summary: Mantis Standart, nicknamed Xiaobai, is a modular wheeled humanoid robot developed by Blue Worm in Xi'an, China. It is designed for research, data collection, and light industrial work, standing 140 cm tall and weighing 50 kg. The robot features two articulated arms, an adjustable waist, and supports up to 22 degrees of freedom for tasks like sorting and assembling. It is supported by ROS 2, MoveIt 2, and VR teleoperation, offering an accessible entry point into wheeled humanoid development. The platform is listed as in production with a starting price of US$1,400.

items.title: Ep#114: Oopsie Data
items.summary: Most existing robotics data consists only of successful robot behaviors. Research areas like world models and reward model learning require examples of failure, such as unsuccessful manipulation trajectories. Claas Voelcker, Arpit Bahety, and Paul Zhou are presenting their work on "oopsie data," which involves collecting these valuable failures. Their goal is to create the first large, community-driven open-source dataset of failure examples. This effort aims to provide necessary data for advancing robotics research.

items.title: What Is Worken? AGIBOT’s Proposed Measure of Productive Robot Work
items.summary: Worken is a proposed measure of productive robot operation combining the number of active robots, autonomous working hours, and an output efficiency ratio. It differentiates independent task execution from nonproductive periods like waiting or manual intervention. The formula multiplies these three factors to calculate "Effective Intelligent Work Hours." This measure is not a price for robot labor and requires defining task-specific benchmarks for accurate results. Practical use depends on consistent operational data and further testing to establish reliable definitions.

items.title: Bleu Robotics raises €5 million to scale humanoid robot deployment in factories
items.summary: Bleu Robotics raised €5 million in a pre-seed round to scale its AI models for industrial humanoid robots. The company aims to reduce the humanoid robot deployment process to one hour or less. Bleu Robotics uses an abductive learning model that allows robots to learn new tasks from just ten operator demonstrations, eliminating the need for vast training datasets. This approach enables cost-effective and scalable deployment by circumventing the need for long training cycles. The technology allows operators to teach robots new tasks directly using handheld devices, facilitating easier deployment in manufacturing settings.
